These petitions are filed seeking a writ of mandamus for a direction to the respondents to initiate the acquisition proceedings in respect of the petitioners' property bearing CTS.No.1126/1-C (1126/C), Ward No.2 situated at Mahatma NC: 2023:KHC-K:9093 Gandhi Road, Vijayapura in WP.No.24497/2016 and CTS.No.1738/1A/2, Ward No.5 situated at Basaveshwar Circle, Main Road,
Bijapur in WP.No.202702/2015.

sentences.text: In WP.No.24497/2016: It is the case of the petitioner that he is the owner in possession and enjoyment of the property bearing CTS.No.1126/1-C (1126/C).
The petitioner claims to have constructed three floor building (Ground+Two floors) by investing lakhs of rupees and several business establishments run in the building.
He has also claimed that the building is furnished with modern amenities, electronic gadgets and fixtures so as to provide proper and competitive services to the customers.

It is the case of the petitioner that it is a Co-operative Society registered under the Karnataka Co-operative Societies Act, 1959, engaged in the business of banking having long standing reputation and huge turnover.
It is catering to the financial and credit requirements of the people of Bijapur.
It is situated in the property bearing CTS.No.1738/1A/2.
The petitioner has constructed three floored building (Ground + Two floors) by investing crores of rupees.
The building is furnished with modern amenities, NC: 2023:KHC-K:9093 electronic gadgets and fixtures so as to provide proper and competitive services to the customers.

4. When such being the case, respondent No.4- Corporation with an intention to implement the Master plan of the year 2006 and to widen the main road (Mahatma Gandhi Road) to an extent of 100 feet (30 metres), it stated to have high handedly demolished the land of adjoining land owners and illegally threatened to demolish the properties belonging to the petitioners.

5. This high handed action of respondent No.4 of illegal demolition and threat to demolish the property belonging to the petitioners and similarly placed private parties were challenged in these writ petitions by seeking a writ of mandamus for a direction to the respondents-authorities to initiate appropriate proceedings for acquisition of the property belonging to the petitioners and pay compensation and thereafter, take possession of the property.

6. During the pendency of these writ petitions, it is contended by learned counsel that the properties of the petitioners along with other adjacent owners of adjoining lands NC: 2023:KHC-K:9093 have been demolished and the possession has been taken by respondent No.4 for formation of road,
which has been completed.

It is also contented by learned counsel that respondent No.4 had issued notice to the petitioners calling upon the petitioners to express their willingness to accept the compensation of Rs.16,56,766.80 to an extent of 251.89 sq.ft. in WP.No.204497/2016 and Rs.41,46,512 to an extent of 330 sq.ft. in WP.No.202702/2015 of the properties belonging to the petitioners, which is required for widening the road.

The petitioners cooperated with respondent No.4 as the properties were required for widening of the road, which is for public purpose and agreed for the properties to be taken for widening of the road, but they have agreed to the same subject to the condition that suitable compensation would be paid in consonance with the market rate prevalent as on the date of the taking possession of the properties belonging to the petitioners.
Hence, the amount that was offered by respondent No.4 was received under protest without prejudice to the rights of the petitioners.

7. This being the state of affairs, some of the adjoining owners and land losers approached this Court in NC: 2023:KHC-K:9093 WP.No.200660/2016 connected with several other writ petitions and the said writ petitions were disposed of and a compromise was arrived at by awarding higher Bijapur District Central Co-Operative ... vs The State Of Karnatka And Ors on 7 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176487885/
4 compensation.

sentences.text:
The petitioners have approached this Court and in these writ petitions, admittedly,
the properties of the petitioners have been taken for construction of the road which the petitioners do not object to.

However, what is questioned is that whether the suitable compensation is paid and the acquisition process is completed in accordance with law, as no process of acquisition is initiated by the respondents.

8. Learned counsel for petitioners contends that pursuant to filing of the petitions, similarly placed land losers of adjoining lands have filed a writ petition in WP.No.206277/2016 connected with other writ petitions, which came to be disposed of by this Court vide order dated 11.07.2023.
The sum and substance of the matters disposed of as stated supra is the same as the one which is agitated before this Court with similar prayers sought for in these petitions.

Therefore, placing reliance and taking into consideration the order passed in the aforementioned writ petition dated 11.07.2023, the petitioners seek disposal of these writ petitions in the similar lines.

Learned counsel for respondent No.4-Corporation contends that the orders passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court in WP.No.206277/2016 and connected with other writ petitions have been taken up in an appeal, which is pending adjudication before the Division Bench of this Court.

He also contends that the petitioners herein would not fall within the same category of the land losers as mentioned in the writ petitions stated hereinabove, wherein each of the petitioners fall in different categories and would not be entitled to similar compensation as the property value would be diminished.

However, he also submits that the possession of the properties of the petitioners along with other writ petitioners mentioned hereinabove have been taken and formation of the road is complete, which is not in dispute.
10. I have heard learned counsel for both parties.
Admittedly, the properties of the petitioners and similarly situated persons have been taken away by respondent No.4 for widening of the road to an extent of 100 feet.

This act of taking away the properties belonging to the petitioners has been done without initiating any process of acquisition under the relevant acts and it is also the fact that some of the land losers have NC: 2023:KHC-K:9093 been paid compensation by way of compromise and consent and some of the petitioners have accepted and received the compensation under protest.
What has to be compensated to each of the petitioners on the basis of norms set out by the respondents will have to be decided by the respondents.
However, the same cannot be contrary to the Act and settled law in force.

11. It is the grievance of the petitioners that though they have accepted certain amount, they have received the said amount under protest and they have now consented by way of compromise and that would be the final amount of compensation for the lands taken away by the respondents.

It is a settled law that when the statutory authorities, for that matter, any authority takes away the land of the private citizens, it will have to be done in accordance with law and the statute, of course, the same cannot be forcibly taken away as it will be contrary to the acts and the laws made by the Legislature.
